fixes: Only rank zero needs checkpoint filesystem access when broadcasting; DTensor strict key validation is consistent across ranks.
DTensor loading honors requested dtype; dense checkpoint broadcast preserves custom non-tensor extra state.
Missing tied aliases use loaded weights rather than stale initialization, including mixed disk/CPU placement.
Int8 offload releases bitsandbytes layer caches as well as parameter storage after each forward.
Layerwise casting shares one lifecycle for recursive and direct-tensor casts.
Memory estimates include tensors owned by parent modules and FP32 Adam state for lower-precision training.
limitations: All real accelerator-device execution (CUDA, XPU, NPU, MPS and others), multi-device transfer, and non-Gloo collectives remain unverified in this CPU environment.
The allocator preserves budgets, tied groups and indivisible layers but uses an independent heuristic; identical maps or peak memory to upstream are not claimed.
Quantization parity covers bitsandbytes 0.48.2 CPU: resident and meta-initialized 4/8-bit models plus repeated 8-bit disk offload. GPU kernels and every quantization recipe remain unverified.
DTensor workflows cover a two-rank CPU mesh with row sharding and full ordinary checkpoint shards, not every FSDP/DTensor topology or serialized distributed-tensor format.
CPU and disk tiers in mixed 4-bit maps retain dense layers by design; 4-bit quantized disk state is not exercised.
These independent workflow samples provide evidence of behavior, not a proof of complete upstream API equivalence.
post_validation_cleanup: Removed two unused imports; module imports and syntax parsing passed after cleanup.
